title: Equal-arm lever
prompt: Push down on an equal-arm lever to lift a 72 N load. The input falls 0.24 m while the load rises 0.24 m. Find the input force.
note: Equal arms give equal vertical distances and equal forces. The lever changes the direction of the force.
change: input and output travel equally far

title: A longer lever arm
prompt: Lift a 320 N load. The input end falls 0.60 m while the load rises 0.15 m. Find the input force.
note: The long arm moves four times as far vertically. It needs one quarter of the load force. The curved trace is the endpoint path; the vertical arrows are the work distances.

title: Balance a seesaw
prompt: A 360 N weight sits 0.60 m right of the fulcrum. What downward force, 1.80 m left of the fulcrum, balances it? In a slow tilt, the left side falls 0.45 m and the right side rises 0.15 m.
note: At rest, both distances and both works are zero. Balance means equal turning effects: F1 × 1.80 = 360 × 0.60. A slow tilt connects this to the work equation using vertical distances.

title: Inclined plane
prompt: Push a 300 N load up a frictionless ramp at steady speed. It travels 2.40 m along the ramp and rises 0.40 m. Find the force parallel to the ramp.
note: Input distance is along the ramp, not its horizontal base. Output work is the increase in gravitational potential energy: weight × vertical rise.
change: input path along the ramp is longer

title: Fixed pulley
prompt: A fixed pulley lifts an 84 N load. Pull down 0.35 m of rope to lift the load 0.35 m. Find the pull force.
note: A fixed pulley changes direction. One rope segment supports the load, so there is no force advantage in this ideal model.
change: input and output travel equally far

title: Movable pulley
prompt: Two rope segments support a 180 N load on a movable pulley. Pull 0.80 m of rope to raise the load 0.40 m. Find the pull force.
note: Two equal-tension rope segments support the load. The free end moves twice as far as the load to keep rope length constant. The pulley and rope are treated as massless.

title: Wheel and axle
prompt: Turn the large wheel to lift a 240 N load using its axle. Your hand travels 0.96 m around the rim while the axle winds up 0.12 m of rope. Find the tangential input force.
note: The wheel and axle turn through the same angle. A larger input radius gives a longer input path. A freely rolling wheel alone is not automatically a force multiplier.
change: hand travels farther around the wheel

title: Geared winch
prompt: A 12-tooth input gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The input crank and output winding drum have equal radii. A 24 N input force moves through 0.80 m; the rope rises 0.20 m. Find the output force.
note: The larger gear turns one quarter as far and has four times the torque. Equal crank and drum radii turn this torque ratio into a force ratio. The forces between the meshing teeth themselves are equal.
change: input crank path is longer than rope travel

title: Screw lift
prompt: Turn a screw handle once. Your hand travels 0.24 m around its circle while a guided platform rises 0.006 m. The load is 600 N. Find the tangential input force.
note: The rotating screw stays at the same height. Its guided nut/platform cannot rotate, so it rises by one thread lead per turn. Thread friction is ignored here.
change: circular input path is much longer

title: A moving wedge
prompt: Push a one-sided wedge horizontally with 65 N to lift a 390 N load by 0.020 m. How far must the wedge move horizontally?
note: A wedge is a moving inclined plane. This load is guided vertically. Use the wedge's horizontal travel and the load's vertical rise, not the sloped-face length.

title: Linked syringes
prompt: Two sealed, water-filled syringes are connected. Push the small plunger with 18 N through 0.16 m. The large plunger moves 0.040 m. Find the output force.
note: The large piston has four times the cross-sectional area. Equal liquid volume means A1d1 = A2d2; equal pressure means F1/A1 = F2/A2. This is a hydraulic machine, not one of the six classical simple machines.

title: Run it in reverse
prompt: Drive a small axle with a tangential input force of 200 N over 0.080 m. The larger wheel produces a 40 N tangential output force. Find the output distance.
note: Now the output moves farther and the output force is smaller. MA is less than 1: a distance/speed advantage, with a force disadvantage. A bigger input force can move a smaller output force farther.
